The standard electrode potential of a half-reaction is the potential at which the reaction is at equilibrium. The standard electrode potential of the hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell is the potential at which the reaction is at equilibrium. The reaction is:

H2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) ightarrow H2O(l)

The standard Gibbs free energy of formation (∆G^0_f)of H2O(l) = -56,690 cal/mole. Therefore the standard electrode potential of the hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell is equal to the standard Gibbs free energy of formation of water, which is -56,690 cal/mole. The answer is (G).
